plan: [With 4 opponents and a third-price rule, the symmetric equilibrium in a uniform iid setting is linear. Modeling opponents as s(v)=a v and optimizing my expected payoff yields a=(4/3). So I should bid b=(4/3)v. No prior rounds to learn from, values redraw each round, so follow equilibrium strategy. For my private value v=$24, equilibrium bid is (4/3)*24 = $32. This maximizes my expected surplus in the long run against similar bidders. ]

[Assuming symmetric bidders use a linear rule b = c·v, solve the best-response condition for a 5-bidder third-price auction. The Bayes–Nash equilibrium gives c = 4/3, so bid b = (4/3)·v. With v = $16, b = 21.333…; round to the allowed $0.1 increment. This strategy maximizes expected profit in repeated play under identical draws.]

[With no past data, assume opponents bid near their values. In a 3rd‑price auction with independent uniform values, bidding my true value is a safe, simple strategy: it wins exactly when my value is highest and yields positive expected surplus (approx 0.4·v conditional on winning). Overbidding risks winning when others' values exceed mine and paying a high 3rd‑price; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With v = $24, I bid my value to capture expected positive profit while avoiding excess risk.]

[ Reason: In a third-price auction with 5 bidders, if I bid high enough to win, I'll pay the second-highest of the four others. Assuming other bids follow values uniformly, the expected second-highest of 4 draws is 3/5*49 ≈ $29.4, giving expected surplus ≈ $17.6. The risk of paying above my value is negligible. So I will bid the maximum $49 to secure the win and maximize expected profit. ]

[This is a third-price sealed-bid with 5 bidders and my private value v = 42. I will bid my true value. Bidding 42 is safe: if I win I pay the third-highest bid which cannot exceed my winning bid, so I will not pay more than my value. Overbidding risks negative payoff; underbidding reduces chances to capture positive surplus. With no informative history and independent draws, truthful bidding maximizes expected long-run profit as a prudent strategy.]
